investigations.name: rate-yield-strategist-competition
investigations.title: Rate- vs Yield-Strategist competition: reproducing Cockx et al. 2024, Fig. 5
investigations.question:
Cockx et al. 2024 (PLOS Comp Biol, "Is it selfish to be filamentous in
biofilms?") introduce iDynoMiCS 2.0 and demonstrate it on a classic
microbial-ecology question: does a Rate Strategist (faster growth, lower
yield) or a Yield Strategist (slower growth, higher/more efficient yield)
win a head-to-head competition for a single limiting substrate — and does
the answer depend on how densely the two strategies are seeded? Can
viva-biofilm's Rust + process-bigraph engine, extended with per-species
kinetics and a distributed multi-strategy spawner, reproduce that
competition and its density-dependence?

investigations.name: viva-biofilm-capabilities
investigations.title: viva-biofilm capabilities: spatial structure, performance, and composability
investigations.question:
Beyond well-mixed equivalence to the reference model (the viva-biofilm-equivalence
investigation), what does the viva-biofilm Rust + process-bigraph engine
make possible that the Java tool does not: fast, deterministic spatial
biofilm simulation with beautiful interactive visuals, measured performance
scaling, and composability with external control processes?

investigations.name: viva-biofilm-equivalence
investigations.title: viva-biofilm: equivalence to a published biofilm model and viva-native capabilities
investigations.question:
Can a clean-room Rust reimplementation of a published individual-based biofilm model (Cockx et al. 2024),
wrapped as viva processes, reproduce the real engine's aggregate observables
while unlocking composability, performance, reproducibility and rich visuals?
